 Social Security benefits to rise 3.6% in 2027 
 Dani Tietz 1 week ago 0 1 minute read 
 Facebook 
 X

 Tumblr

 Reddit 
 VKontakte 
 Odnoklassniki 
 Pocket 
 Social Security benefits will increase 3.6% in 2027, adding an average of $75 a month to retirement benefits, the Social Security Administration announced Wednesday, Oct. 14.
 Nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will receive the cost-of-living adjustment beginning in January. About 7.3 million people who receive Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, will begin receiving higher payments Dec. 31, 2026. Some people receive benefits through both programs.
 The $75 monthly increase is an average for retirement benefits, not a flat increase for every recipient. Beneficiaries will receive personalized notices detailing their new payment amounts, payment dates and any deductions, according to the agency.
 The increase is intended to help beneficiaries keep pace with inflation, rather than provide a gain in purchasing power. Whether it fully offsets rising costs will depend on each household’s expenses and deductions, including Medicare premiums.
 People with personal my Social Security accounts can view their cost-of-living adjustment notices online beginning in late November, up to three weeks before paper notices arrive. Those who have not enrolled in paperless notices will receive their notices by mail in December.
 People without an account must create one and enroll in paperless notices by Nov. 18 to access their notices online, the agency said. Account holders can also request text or email alerts when their notices become available in the account’s Message Center.
 For Medicare enrollees, information about their 2027 premium amounts will be available through the my Social Security Message Center beginning in late November. The personalized benefit notices will identify any deductions from payments.
 Federal law ties the annual cost-of-living adjustment, commonly called the COLA, to changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers. The index is calculated by the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics.
 The adjustment compares the index’s average level in July, August and September with its average during the same three months of the previous year. That formula determines the annual percentage increase in benefits.
